goal: Reduce the game's own browser workload and adapt automatically; user OS/GPU configuration is not the primary remedy.

changes.automaticQuality: Web players start at a conservative tier, including sessions with a saved High preference. Two slow 2-second windows reduce one tier. Recovery requires 20 seconds of stable target-rate frames. Scene loads and focus changes reset observations without discarding the learned tier. The selected quality is the ceiling, not a requirement to render beyond the device budget.
changes.rendering: Web default uses 1x MSAA, a 20-unit shadow distance, 512 shadow atlas, at most 2 additional lights, quarter-resolution bloom with 3 iterations. Lowest visual quality removes point lights/bloom/HDR/shadows. UI resolution stays separate from the 3D render scale.
changes.hud: Apply skill HUD settings on preference/scene changes instead of 20 times per second. Reuse uppercase key labels until the binding changes. Cooldown sampling and skill descriptions that reflect copied skills remain current.
changes.fullscreen: The in-game settings button now uses the same Escape-preserving browser controller as the HTML button.
changes.simulation: No combat, physics, input or network rates were lowered. Windows visual preferences retain their previous behavior.

inspection.editorTimingLimit: A native Editor Login sample on RTX 5060 measured about 1.04 ms main-thread and 1.17 ms GPU time. This is not a browser gameplay benchmark and is not evidence of a Web FPS improvement.
inspection.characterInspection: Imported meshes range from 16,636 to 75,169 triangles. PicoChan's large native uncompressed texture footprint is not used to infer a Web leak: existing WebGL overrides already request compressed textures. No meshes or rig proportions were modified.

coverage: Sustained 30 FPS under a 60 FPS target automatically lowers rendering tiers.
Very slow active devices still lower quality rather than treating every frame as loading.
Background tabs, startup and isolated hitches do not cause an immediate reduction.
Stable recovery respects the user's quality ceiling and does not oscillate after a short recovery.
30 FPS preferences are not mistaken for slow performance.
Runtime pipeline changes do not mutate the source asset.
1,000 unchanged SkillUI updates allocate less than 4 KB and a new binding still updates immediately.
Existing settings, HUD lifecycle and native network/frame-rate tests pass.

limitations: The 36% figure describes a 3D pixel ceiling reduction, not measured FPS or total GPU work reduction.
No claim that every device will run without lag. Default-setting browser gameplay and multiplayer profiling remain necessary.
No new WebGL build or deployment was started; final player testing remains pending the user's build approval.
